text:
Nina R: noticed a repeat pattern in the telemetry - a lot of short-lived service-account exchanges (TTL < 4m) generating noisy quota attributions across projects. proposal: treat very-short TTLs as "fastpath" and route them to a dedicated execution pool with stricter attribution rules.
Harish S: high-level ok. where does the TTL check live? auth-proxy? token-introspect?
Nina R: auth-proxy makes sense because we need routing decision before we hit allocator. token introspect can return ttl, proxy checks and tags request.fastpath=true.
Ben P: what do you mean by stricter attribution rules? assign billing to issuer? to the exchanging project?
Nina R: plan is issuer_project only (the project that minted the short token). no rebinding to downstream projects, and do not roll these into long-term per-project aggregates unless explicit mapping exists.
Maya L: console concerns: users will see requests charged weirdly. we should show a small inline note on the request timeline: "fastpath routing - charged to issuer" with a link. also provide a toggle on billing exports to include/exclude fastpath.
Harish S: metrics we need: auth.fastpath_count, auth.fastpath_route, pool.fastpath_util, auth.fastpath_attr_source. traces should include decision_reason and original_issuer_project (hashed by default).
Ben P: quota enforcement: enforcement points must accept an attribution_override field so we can bill against issuer_project even when derived project is present. do we change existing enforcement API?
Nina R: minimal change: enforcement checks request.context.attribution_override first, fallback to derived project. we'll pass override when fastpath tag is set.
Maya L: privacy: in org-shared dashboards we should mask issuer_project unless user has view_billing permission. show hashed_project_id to others.
Harish S: edge cases: what if pool fastpath is saturated? fallback behavior options: (A) stall and return 503 to preserve attribution semantics; (B) route to normal pool but mark as fastpath_fallback; (C) try to spill to a reserved burst bucket. I prefer B with a hard limit on spill count and an observable metric fastpath_spill_count.
Ben P: agree B is pragmatic. important we still tag traces so investigators can separate pure fastpath vs spilled ones. telemetry event names: auth.fastpath_routed, auth.fastpath_spilled, auth.fastpath_rejected.
Maya L: rollout plan: behind ff_ttl_fastpath. Start internal-only (org:redwood-internal) at 2%. then non-prod tenants 20%, then hosted 100% after a week. For Dedicated/private, gate behind opt-in per-customer until we validate isolation.
Nina R: config example for auth-proxy: 
```yaml
rules:
  - name: fastpath-ttl
    match: token.ttl_seconds < 240
    action:
      route_pool: fastpath-pool
      attribution: issuer_only
      tag: fastpath=true
```
Harish S: need health checks and capacity signals: pool.fastpath_util > 85% should flip behavior to spill, and > 95% should set temporary reject. emit pool.fastpath_util and pool.fastpath_headroom.
Ben P: security note: do NOT bypass scope or consent checks. fastpath only changes the routing/attribution layer. also need to ensure cross-org delegation tokens that are intentionally short-lived keep consent metadata attached.
Maya L: console UX follow-ups: add a filter in Trace Viewer for fastpath=true, add billing export header column fastpath_tag, and include a short FAQ entry. Also a note in SLA that fastpath is best-effort during bursts.
Nina R: tasks: Harish to add proxy TTL matcher + metrics, Ben to wire enforcement to prefer attribution_override, Maya to spec console annotations + permissions masking, I'll write RFC draft and include rollout checklist.
Harish S: I'll post a telemetry PR with the metric names and example dashboards.
Ben P: I'll prototype the enforcement change and a compatibility shim for older enforcers.
deploy-bot: starting deploy for ff_ttl_fastpath at 6490001285 - canary: org:redwood-internal 2%
Maya L: I'll sketch the Trace Viewer badge and billing toggle by EOD and share mocks.
Nina R: thanks team. please add any missing failure modes (token replay, clock skew, issuer impersonation) to the RFC.
